I have worked this land since I was a boy, learning from my father and watching the neighbors. This plot is small — not even a quarter of a hectare — and it is rented, so I will not haul manure here or spend money on new seed or chemicals. But I did give my neighbor some cash to share a bag of DAP from the cooperative, and I will put a few tin-cans full into the soil when I plant, because wheat grows thin and weak without it. I am using my own seed that I saved from last harvest, and my wife and I will do all the work with our oxen — ploughing, planting, weeding, and harvest — about fifteen days of our own labor, with no hired hands.
